headline: South Asia: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media.
- Western Russia: One killed and 37 injured in Russian attacks on Kherson in a single day.
- Africa: Iran denies being behind Houthi attacks as Aden airport hit.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
- Military Times, one day ago: US Army’s 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated.
The Army's 8th Psychological Operations Group inactivated as the service reshapes its PSYOP and information warfare forces to counter global adversaries.
- Military Times, one day ago: What is the US Army doing in Panama? A bit of everything..
As Washington shifts its attention toward the Western Hemisphere, a reinvigorated jungle school is just one part of the evolving U.S. presence in Panama.
- Military Times, one day ago: ‘Weaponized light’: KBR’s new base defense technology pits lasers against drones.
The Pentagon recently selected KBR's Firefly system for a pilot program to test defending U.S. military installations against adversarial drones.
The Caribbean - bottom line: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: 19-y-o charged with Kidd Lane triple murder.
A 19-year-old man has been charged with three counts of murder in connection with last Friday’s deadly attack on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, which claimed the lives of two women and a one-year-old boy. The accused, Dante Davis, who has addresses on Spanish Town Road and Kidd Lane in Kingston 13, is also facing charges of conspiracy to commit murder, arson, conspiracy to commit arson, possession of a prohibited weapon, unauthorised possession of ammunition and using a firearm to commit a felony.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA

Russian forces launched airstrikes, artillery bombardments and drone attacks on Kherson Oblast on 17 October, leaving one person dead and 40 others injured, including 37 in the city of Kherson.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Found under rubble by his colleagues: Ukrainian emergency worker killed in Russian strike on Donetsk Oblast.
Anatolii Hopka, 41, a rescue worker with the State Emergency Service of Ukraine, has been killed in a Russian airstrike on a residential building in Sloviansk.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Kromberg & Schubert plant in Lutsk halts operations following Russian strikes.
The Kromberg & Schubert plant in Lutsk, which manufactures onboard electrical cable systems for cars, has suspended operations following Russian strikes on the facility.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Zelenskyy says Russia wants to deploy ballistic missile systems in Belarus to attack Ukraine's west.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stated that Russia intends to deploy ballistic missile systems in Belarus to attack the western part of Ukraine.

Iran has denied any involvement in an escalation of attacks by Houthi rebels on Saudi targets. The international airport in Yemen’s interim capital Aden was struck by two missiles late on Friday, the second such incident in less than two weeks.

Attacks hit several areas as UNICEF reports more than 340 children killed since 'ceasefire' began a year ago.

NATO member Romania shares a border with Ukraine, much of it along the Danube, and has repeatedly reported Russian drone incursions into its airspace since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Media Statement - Defence Committee Calls for Urgent Action to Reverse SANDF Decline.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, one day ago: South Africa: Katherine O'regan Receives George Bizos Human Rights Award, Warns of Shift to Authoritarianism.
[Daily Maverick] On 15 October, former Constitutional Court Justice Katherine O'Regan received the George Bizos Human Rights Award, reflecting on the project of democracy and urging resistance to rising authoritarianism.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media.
Security forces have responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Upper Kurram, state broadcaster PTV News reported on Saturday. PTV News and state-run Associated Press of Pakistan (APP), which cited security sources, said the Afghan Taliban forces opened fire to “facilitate terrorists” along the border in Taldah sector of Upper Kurram. The army responded using heavy weapons, destroying several Afghan Taliban posts and forcing their personnel to flee from there, PTV News reported.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran supports a “political process” to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi rebels. The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a major attack last week. “We support an inclusive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue,” Araghchi said in a speech at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Trump-Zelenskiy rift threatens vital support for Kyiv.
From US threats to cut off intelligence support for Ukraine to a diesel deal that could help Russia fund its war, it has been a damaging week for ties between Kyiv and its most important ally, Washington. Frustrated by high energy costs he blames partly on Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, US President Donald Trump has repeatedly criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. A disruption of US-provided satellite internet services raised fears that Ukraine could be vulnerable as it prepares for another winter of Russian attacks on its energy infrastructure.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump.
President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine. The move came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders to keep financing Kyiv’s fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, insisting he was standing up for his country as Trump’s support slumped.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: Man killed, four injured in suspected militant attack on Kuki village in Manipur.
A tragic incident unfolded in Chassad village, Manipur, where a militant attack led to the death of one man and injuries to four others. Gunfire erupted between the militants and a local armed faction, with the violence persisting into the evening. Emergency services promptly transported the injured to a hospital, but sadly, one victim did not survive.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: The Next War Could Begin In Space Within 5 Years, Experts Warn.
A major attack on satellites could disrupt GPS, internet services, television broadcasts, weather forecasting and air traffic control. Banking and other essential services could also suffer, potentially bringing modern life to a standstill.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 17 hours ago: 'I love you' on clothes & a chilling note: What preceded Gurgaon techie couple's deaths.
An IT professional, Mohammad Aslam, and his wife, Farhana, were discovered dead in their Gurgaon apartment. Aslam sent an alarming email to his employer before the incident, indicating a distressing situation. Police suspect that Aslam may have killed his wife before taking his own life. Relatives claim that Aslam had been struggling with depression for about 18 months prior to the tragedy.

Australia - bottom line: Starlink speed restrictions ground interceptors as Russian strikes batter Ukraine.

Ukraine is grappling with Starlink restrictions vital to operating its interceptors as Trump pauses some Russian sanctions.
- The Guardian - Australia, one hour ago: Hiding in plane sight: the invisible turbulence that can strike out of a clear blue sky.
As the planet warms, airlines are grappling with what this means for air travel – and for the passengers who simply refuse to keep their seatbelts fastened It was a swelteringly hot afternoon in south-west Myanmar on 21 May 2024. Tropical thunderstorms, showers and highs of 36C were forecast for the area around the Irrawaddy Basin. High above, monsoonal heat and humidity were building into a vast convective column of water vapour, a towering cumulonimbus cloud soaring up to 35,000ft (more than 10,500 metres) into the air.
